Wherever commodities are desired and cannot be obtained legally, a criminal element providing those commodities usually springs up. The entrance to the bay was blocked by two large barrier islands, Grand Tier and Grand Isle, that made passage by larger vessels difficult, if not impossible. By early 1809, it became well known throughout New Orleans that if you wanted to purchase goods you couldn't legally get anywhere else, all you had to do was take a small boat out to Baritaria and visit the establishment presided over by the notorious Captain Lefit. As the '90s approached, the lackluster results of Gorbachev's reforms, the tension across the Soviet states, and the issues at home, in particular in Politureau, were becoming insurmountable. There had been warning signs of what was potentially coming for Gorbachev for almost a year. His more trusted inner circle had been asking for Gorbachev to be more proactive and declare a state of emergency, but he'd refused. It was August 1991. Mikail and Rya were in Crimea on holiday and would return on August 20th to sign the new union treaty which was to redefine the Soviet Union allowing for more state autonomy while remaining in the union. On August 17th, a group of men who became known as the Gang of Eight with Vice President Gennady Yaniv as a member met at a KGB guest house in Moscow where they denounced the treaty. They felt it would be the USSR's undoing, so they decided to take matters into their own hands. On August 18th, they flew to Crimea and detained Gorbachev in his DACA. They took control of the USSR and claimed Gorbachev was ill, which was of course a lie. The events of the coup were spread over 3 days, and since he was detained in Crimea, Gorbachev's story of the event is almost unimportant. It's more Yeltson's story, as this was his true rise to power. The coup, while brief, had dire ramifications. By the end of the year, communism, the USSR, and Gorbachev's career were all dead and buried with Gorbachev fully resigning by December 25th. The collapse of the USSR would have likely happened eventually. But Gorbachov's efforts to reform a broken system exposed it for what it was, a broken [Music] system. Life after power was not easy for Gorbachev in a country that didn't like him and a world that didn't need him. Initially, he worked on his foundation, which he founded in December 1991, which focused on presenting ideas for a democratic Russia and its future. He lectured around the world and made good money doing so, wrote a book, and even did some strange ads for companies that had just set up shop in Russia, like Pizza Hut. After initially vowing not to criticize Yeltson's presidency, he eventually lambasted the president over reforms that led to inflation and widespread poverty. This led him to doing something nobody believed he should do, run for president. He announced his candidacy on March 1st, 1996. Running as an independent, Gorbachev faced challenges like a lack of media coverage surrounding the campaign and a general public hatred for Gorbachev. Winning was never going to happen. And in a way, he knew that. It's unclear if his intentions were focused on rehabilitating his image or if he truly believed in his campaign. Regardless, his bid failed. In total, Gorbachev received.5% of the total vote in round one and came seventh out of 11 candidates with Yeltson ultimately winning. In July 1999, tragedy struck Gorbachev when his wife Raisa was diagnosed with leukemia. She was treated in Germany but fell into a coma in September, dying shortly after. Miky vowed never to marry again, a promise he kept. In December 1999, Yeltson resigned from the presidency and Vladimir Putin took over before being officially elected president in May 2000. In a way, Gorbachev and Putin shared many similar beliefs. Gorbachev was critical of US attitudes to the end of the cold war, especially their talking points of winning a war without winners. He was critical of their attitude towards Putin. He was anti-NATO expansion and activities, especially the Iraq war. Starting in 2008, Gorbachev slowly became more critical of Putin, which only increased yearbyear. Gorbachev lived to see the start of the Ukraine war, but opted to remain relatively quiet on the subject. His foundation relayed that they affirmed the need for an early sessation of hostilities and immediate start of peace negotiations. There is nothing more precious in the world than human lives. Additionally, Miky's interpreter stated that Gorbachev was traumatized by the invasion in the months leading up to his death. On August 30th, 2022, Miky Gorbashov died at the age of 91 in Moscow due to a severe prolonged illness. The last decade of his life in particular was spent in and out of the hospital undergoing numerous surgeries, some minor and some more complex. Perhaps the most telling of Gorbachev's legacy is how differently everyone interprets it. Westerners have a false belief that Gorbachev was liberal, but that wasn't true. He had no desire to see the USSR fall. He just wanted to reform it, improve it, but ultimately keep it intact. By all accounts, the fall of the Soviet Union was an accident. Look to Gorbachev's response to separatists in Latafia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, and Lithuania as proof. It was chaos and bloodshed which could have gone further if not for the threat of nuclear fallout and civil war. Despite his humiliating end as a leader, he continued collecting numerous awards around the world, including the Nobel Peace Prize, which he was conflicted about receiving. At home, he was far from loved both in Russia and across the former Soviet states. One of the people who hated him the most was and remains Putin. He blames Gorbachev for the USSR's collapse. Yeltson may have made it official with the 1991 Ballayosh Accords, but to Putin, it was Gorbachev who shouldered the blame. While his legacy is different depending on who you ask and how you feel, it shadow remains as Putin attempts to rebuild the world Gorbachev destroyed. I hope you learned something today. I'm Eric Malikite, and we'll see you next time. [Music]
